title: Peloton Bike Not Connecting to Tablet
shortDescription: Tablet fails to detect the bike, resistance and cadence do not display.
fullDescription:
The Peloton Bike communicates with the touchscreen tablet via an internal cable that sends resistance and cadence data. When the tablet cannot read bike metrics, it usually means a loose cable, faulty sensor, or software glitch is preventing pairing.

This is one of the most common Peloton issues and is often resolved by reseating the cable behind the tablet or performing a software restart. On Bike+, the connection is more robust but cable wear can still occur.

causes.cause: Loose cable connection behind the tablet

fixSteps.title: Restart the tablet
fixSteps.instruction: Hold the power button for 10 seconds until the tablet reboots.

fixSteps.title: Reseat the cable
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the tablet from the mount and firmly reconnect the cable behind it.

fixSteps.title: Contact Peloton Support
fixSteps.instruction: If the problem persists, request a sensor or cable replacement under warranty.

whenToCallPro: Call Peloton Support if the bike is under warranty or if reseating the cable does not restore connection.
videoSearchQuery: Peloton bike not connecting to tablet fix

faq.a: Yes, Peloton typically covers bike-to-tablet connection issues within the warranty period.

title: Peloton Tablet Will Not Power On
shortDescription: Touchscreen remains black even with power connected.
fullDescription:
A dead Peloton tablet is usually caused by a power adapter fault, a loose power cable inside the bike frame, or a firmware issue. The bike must be plugged into a working outlet and the power cable inside the frame must be seated correctly.

Occasionally a forced reboot using the power button on the rear of the tablet will resolve a frozen or hung boot cycle.

causes.cause: Faulty wall outlet or surge protector

fixSteps.title: Test the outlet
fixSteps.instruction: Plug a lamp or phone charger into the same outlet to verify power.

fixSteps.title: Force reboot
fixSteps.instruction: Hold the power button on the back of the tablet for 20 seconds.

fixSteps.title: Inspect cables
fixSteps.instruction: Check that the power cable is firmly seated at both the tablet and the frame inlet.

whenToCallPro: If the tablet remains dead after testing power and cables, contact Peloton Support for a replacement.
videoSearchQuery: Peloton tablet won't turn on fix

faq.q: Can I use my own charger?
faq.a: No, use only the Peloton-supplied power adapter to avoid damaging the tablet.

title: Peloton Touchscreen Frozen or Unresponsive
shortDescription: Tablet shows image but does not respond to touch.
fullDescription:
A frozen Peloton screen usually comes from a software hang, failed app update, or memory leak during a long session. A forced restart clears RAM and typically restores touch responsiveness.

If freezes recur, a factory reset or software reinstall from the support menu may be required.

fixSteps.title: Force reboot
fixSteps.instruction: Hold power button 10-15 seconds until the tablet restarts.

fixSteps.title: Check for updates
fixSteps.instruction: After reboot, go to Settings and install any pending software updates.

fixSteps.title: Factory reset
fixSteps.instruction: If the issue returns, use Settings > Device Settings > Factory Reset. You will need to sign in again.

whenToCallPro: Contact Peloton Support if freezes continue after a factory reset.

faq.q: Will I lose my ride history?
faq.a: No, ride history is stored in your Peloton account in the cloud.

title: Heart Rate Monitor Will Not Pair to Peloton
shortDescription: Tablet cannot detect Bluetooth or ANT+ heart rate strap.
fullDescription:
Peloton supports most Bluetooth Low Energy and ANT+ heart rate straps. Pairing failures are usually caused by a dead HRM battery, dry contacts on a chest strap, or Bluetooth interference from nearby devices.

Make sure the strap is moistened, the battery is fresh, and no other app (like a phone) has an active connection to the same strap.

causes.cause: Dry skin contacts on chest strap

symptoms: HRM not shown in device list

fixSteps.title: Replace battery
fixSteps.instruction: Install a fresh CR2032 battery in the chest strap.

fixSteps.title: Moisten contacts
fixSteps.instruction: Dampen the conductive pads on the back of the chest strap before wearing.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect other apps
fixSteps.instruction: Close any fitness apps on your phone that might be holding the HRM connection.

fixSteps.title: Re-pair in Peloton settings
fixSteps.instruction: Open Settings > Bluetooth Devices > Scan and select your HRM.

whenToCallPro: If pairing fails with multiple HRMs, the Bluetooth radio on the tablet may need Peloton Support.
videoSearchQuery: Peloton heart rate monitor not pairing

faq.a: Most Bluetooth LE and ANT+ straps work, including Polar, Garmin, and Wahoo.

title: Peloton Resistance Knob Stuck or Skipping
shortDescription: Resistance knob won't turn or does not change displayed resistance.
fullDescription:
On the original Peloton Bike, the resistance knob mechanically moves a magnet assembly against the flywheel. A stuck knob may mean the magnet assembly is seized from lack of use or the knob shaft is bent. On Bike+, resistance is controlled electronically, so a stuck knob usually indicates a failed motor.

Avoid forcing the knob beyond its stops, which can shear the internal linkage.

fixSteps.title: Apply silicone lubricant
fixSteps.instruction: On the Bike, spray silicone (not WD-40) on the magnet assembly guide rods through the knob slot.

fixSteps.title: Test full range
fixSteps.instruction: Slowly turn knob through its full range multiple times to free the mechanism.

fixSteps.title: Contact Peloton
fixSteps.instruction: If the knob remains stuck or you have a Bike+, schedule a service visit.

whenToCallPro: Call Peloton for Bike+ resistance issues or if the shaft is bent on the original Bike.

faq.a: No, use only silicone lubricant. WD-40 attracts dust and may damage the magnet assembly.

title: Peloton Touchscreen Misaligned or Miscalibrated
shortDescription: Touch targets register offset from where you tap.
fullDescription: Touchscreen drift on Peloton tablets is rare but can occur after a firmware update or exposure to heavy sweat. The fix is usually a reboot followed by a factory reset if needed. There is no user-accessible calibration menu.

fixSteps.title: Clean and dry the screen
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe the tablet with a dry microfiber cloth and allow it to fully dry.

fixSteps.title: Reboot tablet
fixSteps.instruction: Hold power button for 10 seconds.

fixSteps.title: Factory reset
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > Device Settings > Factory Reset if issue persists.

whenToCallPro: Contact Peloton if calibration issues persist after factory reset.

faq.a: No, the Peloton OS does not expose a manual calibration tool.

title: Peloton Repeatedly Disconnects from Wi-Fi
shortDescription: Connection drops mid-class or fails to stay connected.
fullDescription:
Peloton classes stream in HD and require a stable Wi-Fi connection. Drops are usually caused by a weak signal, a 2.4 GHz / 5 GHz band conflict, or a router that periodically renews DHCP leases.

Moving the router closer or using a dedicated 5 GHz SSID often resolves buffering and disconnects.

causes.cause: Weak Wi-Fi signal at the bike

fixSteps.title: Test signal strength
fixSteps.instruction: Check Settings > Wi-Fi for signal bars. Less than 2 bars is too weak.

fixSteps.title: Forget and reconnect
fixSteps.instruction: Forget the network, restart the tablet, then reconnect.

fixSteps.title: Add Wi-Fi extender
fixSteps.instruction: If signal is weak, add a mesh node or extender within 20 feet of the bike.

whenToCallPro: Call Peloton Support if Wi-Fi fails only on the tablet while other devices work fine nearby.

faq.a: Peloton Tread+ and some Bike+ units accept USB-to-Ethernet adapters, but Wi-Fi is the primary connection.

title: Peloton Speaker Produces No or Distorted Sound
shortDescription: Audio missing, crackling, or very quiet from built-in speakers.
fullDescription:
The Peloton tablet has two rear-facing speakers. A Bluetooth connection to headphones or a speaker can silently steal audio, which is the most common cause of 'no sound'. Distorted sound usually points to a blown speaker or a cracked driver cable.

Unpair unused Bluetooth devices and check volume settings before assuming hardware failure.

causes.cause: Volume set to zero or muted

fixSteps.title: Unpair Bluetooth audio
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > Bluetooth and disconnect all paired audio devices.

fixSteps.title: Raise volume
fixSteps.instruction: Use the tablet-side volume keys to confirm volume is above 50%.

fixSteps.title: Reboot tablet
fixSteps.instruction: Hold power 10 seconds to clear audio driver state.

whenToCallPro: If only one speaker works or distortion persists, contact Peloton for tablet replacement.

faq.a: Yes, Bluetooth speakers and the 3.5mm headphone jack both work.

title: Peloton Headphone Jack Not Working
shortDescription: Wired headphones produce no sound or cut in and out.
fullDescription:
The 3.5mm headphone jack on the Peloton tablet can collect lint and sweat, causing intermittent detection. A cotton swab with isopropyl alcohol or a blast of compressed air usually clears the socket.

If the plug does not 'click' firmly, the internal spring contact may be worn and the tablet needs service.

causes.cause: Lint or debris in the jack

symptoms: Audio cuts out when cable moves

fixSteps.title: Clean the jack
fixSteps.instruction: Use compressed air or a dry toothpick to remove lint.

fixSteps.title: Test another pair
fixSteps.instruction: Try a different wired headphone set to rule out a bad cable.

fixSteps.title: Use Bluetooth
fixSteps.instruction: As a workaround, pair Bluetooth headphones.

whenToCallPro: Contact Peloton if the jack is physically damaged or loose.

faq.a: Yes, AirPods pair via Bluetooth like any other wireless headphones.

title: Peloton Error C001 - Connection Fault
shortDescription: Internal connection error between tablet and bike electronics.
fullDescription:
Error C001 indicates the tablet cannot establish a data handshake with the bike's main controller. This often appears on Bike+ after a firmware update, and is normally resolved by a power cycle of the entire unit.

If C001 persists, the control board or data cable may need replacement by a Peloton technician.

fixSteps.title: Unplug for 5 minutes
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the bike from the wall for at least 5 minutes to fully drain capacitors.

fixSteps.title: Reconnect and boot
fixSteps.instruction: Plug back in and allow the tablet to complete boot.

fixSteps.title: Contact support
fixSteps.instruction: If C001 returns, open a support ticket - this usually requires a technician visit.

whenToCallPro: C001 almost always requires a Peloton technician for board-level repair.

faq.q: Can I use the bike with C001?
faq.a: No, the tablet cannot record rides until C001 is resolved.

title: Peloton Tread Error E2 - Belt Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Tread belt speed sensor reports invalid data.
fullDescription:
On the Peloton Tread and Tread+, E2 indicates the belt speed sensor is returning out-of-range values. This can be caused by a loose sensor, a belt that has slipped, or motor control board issues.

Because the Tread belt operates at high speed, do not attempt mechanical repair yourself. Stop using the treadmill until a Peloton technician inspects it.

fixSteps.title: Stop using tread
fixSteps.instruction: Do not run until E2 is resolved - this is a safety concern.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off, unplug for 5 minutes, then restart. Sometimes clears transient errors.

fixSteps.title: Schedule service
fixSteps.instruction: Contact Peloton Support to schedule a certified technician visit.

whenToCallPro: Always call Peloton for E2 - do not run the tread until repaired.

faq.a: Yes, within the Tread warranty period Peloton covers this repair.

title: Peloton Error Code 40 - Motor Controller Fault
shortDescription: Motor controller reports an over-current or communication fault.
fullDescription:
Error 40 on Peloton Tread indicates the motor controller has detected an abnormal current draw or lost communication with the main board. This is typically triggered by a stuck belt, worn motor brushes, or a failed capacitor on the controller.

This error requires professional service - stop using the tread immediately.

fixSteps.title: Power off immediately
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the tread from the wall. Do not attempt to run it.

fixSteps.title: Inspect belt by hand
fixSteps.instruction: With tread unplugged, manually rotate the belt. If it binds, do not force it.

fixSteps.title: Contact Peloton
fixSteps.instruction: Open a service ticket - Error 40 almost always requires motor or controller replacement.

whenToCallPro: Always - Error 40 is a safety and electrical concern requiring certified repair.

faq.q: Can I keep using tread at low speed?
faq.a: No, power the unit down and stop use until repaired.
